title: Local dominating member of a finite continuous ultrametric family
statement: Let S be a topological space, E an ultrametric normed field, I a finite type, and a_i:S→E continuous functions. If some a_i(x) is nonzero, there are an open neighborhood U of x and i such that a_i never vanishes on U and every a_j has norm at most the norm of a_i at every point of U.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: Choose a member with maximal norm at x, using Finset.exists_max_image. Its norm is positive.
Intersect the finitely many open sets where each difference from its value at x has norm below that maximum. The ultrametric inequality keeps the chosen norm unchanged and bounds every other norm.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, continuous coefficient framework; analytic matrix-chart reduction
proof_origin.note: The matrix argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument stated in Lemma 6.8.7.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_dominating_member
    {S E I : Type*} [TopologicalSpace S] [NormedField E] [IsUltrametricDist E]
    [Finite I] (a : I → C(S, E)) (x : S) (hx : ∃ i, a i x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (U : Set S) (i : I), IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧
      (∀ y ∈ U, a i y ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ j y, y ∈ U → ‖a j y‖ ≤ ‖a i y‖
